title: How the Japanese COVID-19 Context Alters the Longitudinal Link Between Fine Motor Skills and Expressive Vocabulary in Preschoolers
content: Background/Objective: This study investigated the longitudinal association between early fine motor skills and subsequent expressive vocabulary development within Bronfenbrenner’s ecological systems theory. We examined how an abrupt shift in the macrosystem and chronosystem, specifically the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated social restrictions, affected children’s developmental processes within the microsystem of the home and childcare settings. Method: The participants included 1,199 children (pre-pandemic: n = 731; pandemic: n = 468) who attended licensed childcare centers in Japan. Using hierarchical multiple regression analyses adjusted for baseline demographic characteristics and home-rearing environment (HRE), we examined whether fine motor skills at Time 1 (T1) predicted expressive vocabulary outcomes at a two-year follow-up Time 2 (T2), and whether this association differed by cohort. Result: The primary analysis revealed a significant interaction between cohort and fine motor skills at T1 was observed (b = −0.09, p < .001), indicating that the association between early motor skills and later expressive vocabulary differed between the pre-pandemic and pandemic cohorts. These findings suggest that environmental constraints during the pandemic may have disrupted the typical developmental pathways linking motor and linguistic skills. Conclusion: Reduced social interaction and communication opportunities may limit children’s ability to translate motor exploration into language development. This study highlights the sensitivity of developmental processes to broader ecological disruptions.
